I have your one-pager. Before we go in, give me the whole thing in two sentences.
People leave in the first year because there is no first month. If we pilot a structured onboarding program in one site, early attrition will fall.
How much is this going to cost me?
Almost nothing in the pilot. If it works and we scale it, the investment comes back in the overtime line, not in the training line.
The site managers will tell you their teams are too busy for this.
They will. That is why I need your buy-in first. As long as it comes from you, the conversation with them is short.
And if it does not work?
Then we stop in ninety days and I bring you the reason. Unless attrition falls by five points, there is no second pilot. That is written on the page.
If we pilot it in one site, we will know in ninety days.
Unless we fix the root cause, the number will come back.
As long as I have your buy-in, the rest is a short conversation.
If it does not work, we stop, and I bring you the reason.
I will prepare a second version in case they ask for one.

Adriana, it is Claire. I read your proposal last night and I want it on the agenda, but not in the form it is in now. Two things. First, do not ask for the whole budget at once. If you ask for everything in the first meeting, they will say no in the first meeting. Ask for a pilot in one site. Second, the sentence about the root cause is the strongest thing in the document and it is on page nine. Move it to page one. If they read that paragraph first, they will understand why the initiative exists, and the rest of the proposal will defend itself. One more thing: bring the finance director in before the meeting, not during it. If you have his buy-in beforehand, nobody else in the room will argue with the numbers.

Thank you all for coming. Here is where we are with the onboarding initiative. We are going to pilot it in one site, starting in March, and we will review it in ninety days. If the pilot works, we will scale it to the whole region before the end of the year. If it does not work, we will stop it, and that is a real option, not a formality. The condition is simple: early attrition in that site has to fall by at least five points. Nothing else counts. I want to be clear about one thing, because people always ask. If a manager tells you that his team is too busy for onboarding, send that manager to me. That conversation is mine, not yours.
